title: Where AI Belongs in a Process
description: Diagnosing a business process to find where AI genuinely helps versus where it adds risk or quietly removes judgment a human needs to keep making.

title: What These Systems Can Actually Do
description: What a language model is actually doing when it produces an answer, why fluent output and correct output are different claims, and how to describe current AI capability to a client accurately enough that you only promise what will actually arrive.

title: Rules, AI, or a Person
description: Choosing the right mechanism per process step — a fixed rule, a model, a human, or a cascade of the three — using cost, latency, debuggability and stakes rather than defaulting to whichever mechanism is newest. Most steps that get automated with AI shouldn't be.

title: The Judgement You Can't Remove
description: Identifying the decisions where removing the human transfers real risk onto someone who never agreed to carry it — money, health, or a permanent record — and designing the review step so it actually gets done instead of becoming a rubber stamp under backlog pressure.

title: The Data You Actually Have
description: Judging whether a client's data can actually support the automation being proposed — where it really lives, whether there's enough of it labelled the right way, what may legally leave the building, where it's wrong in a way nobody can see, and what the client already promised its own users about it.

title: Naming the Risk Before You Commit
description: Stating what can go wrong, how badly, and who bears it — in writing, while the client can still say no — instead of discovering the failure mode together after the engagement is signed. Includes when the honest answer is walking away.
